title: WPMS/1628/2019 of DHEERAJ SHARMA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1628 of 2019
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. Suyash Pant, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for
respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
Petitioners are partners in M/s Exsol
Energy System. The said partnership firm
is authorized dealer of Exide batteries,
including Battery Bank and Battery
Chargers, which are used in power
stations. Power Transmission Corporation
of Uttarakhand Limited (PTCUL) issued e-tender inviting bids for supply of Battery
Bank and Battery Chargers. Three bids
were received pursuant to the e-tender
including that of the petitioner. The
technical bid submitted by the petitioner's
firm was rejected on the ground that its
bid did not meet the criteria of the tender
document.
Learned counsel for the petitioners
submits that Technical Evaluation
Committee evaluated technical bids
submitted by the petitioner and, in its
report, Technical Evaluation Committee
had categorically stated that it meets the
T.Q.R.
M/s Costal Gujarat Power Ltd.
(CGPL), whose Experience/Performance
Certificate was relied upon the petitioner,
issued a communication through e-mail
on 30.01.2019 stating that the
Experience/Performance Certificate relied
upon by the petitioner was valid only till

issuance of certificate i.e. January, 2015
and, subsequent to issuance of said
certificate, the Exide batteries supplied by
the dealer are not performing
satisfactorily.
Learned counsel for the petitioners,
on the other hand, submits that, as per
the tender document, each bidder was
required to submit 20 Experience/
Performance Certificates; whereas,
petitioner has enclosed as many as 22
Experience/Performance Certificates
alongwith his technical bid, therefore,
according to him, even if Experience/
Performance Certificate issued by CGPL is
ignored, then also, petitioner was
technically qualified and rejection of his
technical bid is erroneous. He further
submits that life of heavy duty batteries
meant for Electric Sub Stations is six
years and, even if, the communication
issued by CGPL on 30.01.2019 is accepted
as gospel truth, then also it is apparent
that Exide Batteries supplied by the dealer
gave trouble free service upto 2017, as in
the said communication it has been stated
that "over the past two years, we have
been facing issues in battery banks
mentioned in the certificate".
Learned counsel for PTCUL submits
that these aspects can only be decided by
an expert, particularly the issue raised by
the petitioners regarding life of the
batteries.
Since the issue of life of batteries
supplied by the dealer whose Experience
Certificate has been relied upon by the
petitioner is relevant in the matter,
therefore, this aspect can only be looked
into by an expert.

Accordingly, the writ petition is
disposed of with liberty to the petitioners
to make representation to Managing
Director, PTCUL within 48 hours. If such
representation is made within the
stipulated period, Managing Director,
PTCUL shall look into the matter and shall
take appropriate decision, in accordance
with law, within two weeks from the date
of receipt of representation alongwith
certified copy of this order. The said
decision shall also be communicated to
the petitioner.
Till decision is taken by Managing
Director, PTCUL, supply order shall not be
issued.
Let a certified copy of this order be
issued today itself.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Arpan 04.03.2020
